primitives.name: Excess Accuracy
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Headline metric:** excess_acc = model accuracy - always_up accuracy, with block-bootstrap intervals; paired McNemar and Diebold–Mariano tests under Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control.
primitives.assumptions: Model accuracy and always-up accuracy are computed on identical time windows; paired tests ensure independence of observations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model accuracy equals or falls below the base rate, excess accuracy becomes non-positive, indicating no directional edge.

layer2.mapping: Excess accuracy serves as a derived kernel for evaluating directional forecasting skill in GSE's pick scoring system by subtracting the performance of a naive always-up strategy.
layer2.telemetry: Paired McNemar test p-values and block-bootstrapped confidence intervals.

primitives.name: Walk-Forward Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stratified held-out tickers ~80/20 per sector, fixed seed 42, fixed across folds (seen: 76/394; held-out: 24/107).
primitives.assumptions: Historical data is temporally ordered and fold boundaries reflect realistic deployment scenarios.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Validation fails when temporal order is violated or when held-out symbols do not generalize across sectors.

layer2.mapping: The walk-forward scheme mirrors GSE's team-level held-out validation, where expansion teams act as unseen test sets for forecasting generalization.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-fold consistency of excess accuracy metrics and out-of-sample directional hit rates.

primitives.name: Base-Rate Honest Benchmark
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — the equity result itself is a negative result (no directional edge), but the *base-rate-honest evaluation protocol* is the most important methodology import in this lane: GSE's pick hit-rates must be scored against always-up/market base rates with paired tests, or every backtest is a lie.
primitives.assumptions: Always-up represents the minimal viable benchmark in a drifting market; paired testing ensures valid comparison between models and baselines.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when model performance is evaluated without accounting for the base rate, leading to spurious claims of forecasting skill.

layer2.mapping: This primitive underpins GSE's requirement that all pick hit-rates be reported relative to always-up and other market-implied baselines, preventing overfitting to historical noise.
layer2.telemetry: Statistical significance of excess accuracy versus always-up using McNemar and Diebold–Mariano tests.
